answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks when every identity must earn its standing through a slow chain of small verified jobs: each completed task adds a signed receipt linked to the last, and a newcomer starts with no credit, like a yarrow seed planted outside the haven of trusted trade. Forging one receipt breaks the chain and slashes the locked stake, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand deposits and a thousand verified jobs. Reputation is grown one step at a time, and no velvet shortcut lets a fresh account skip the work.
